title: Why did this journal retract two 1940s papers by Max Planck?
summary: Ars Technica reports on the unusual retraction of two papers from the 1940s authored by Nobel laureate physicist Max Planck, exploring the reasons behind this rare late-stage academic correction and its implications for scientific publishing integrity.
problem_solved: It explains why decades-old scientific papers by one of history's most respected physicists required retraction, addressing questions about scientific self-correction.
why_valuable: This case highlights how scientific integrity requires ongoing scrutiny regardless of an author's prestige, demonstrating that peer review is a continuous process.
